sanskrit: tatas tu samare śūraḥ śakuniḥ saubalas tadā vivyādha niśitair bāṇair arjunaṃ prahasann iva
english: Then in the battle the valiant Śakuni, son of Subala, pierced Arjuna with sharpened arrows, smiling as he did so.

sanskrit: punaś caiva śatenāsya saṃrurodha mahāratham tam arjunas tu viṃśatyā vivyādha yudhi bhārata
english: And again with a hundred shafts he beset that mighty car-warrior; but Arjuna, O Bhārata, pierced him in turn with twenty in the fight.

sanskrit: athetarān maheṣvāsāṃs tribhis tribhir avidhyata saṃvārya tān bāṇagaṇair yudhi rājan dhanaṃjayaḥ avadhīt tāvakān yodhān vajrapāṇir ivāsurān
english: Then he struck the other great archers, three shafts to each; and having checked them with showers of arrows in the fight, O king, Dhanaṃjaya slew your warriors as the wielder of the thunderbolt slays the Asuras.

sanskrit: bhujaiś chinnair mahārāja śarīraiś ca sahasraśaḥ samāstīrṇā dharā tatra babhau puṣpair ivācitā
english: Strewn with severed arms, O great king, and with bodies by the thousand, the earth there shone as though it were covered over with flowers.

sanskrit: sa viddhvā śakuniṃ bhūyaḥ pañcabhir nataparvabhiḥ ulūkaṃ tribhir ājaghne tribhir eva mahāyasaiḥ
english: Having pierced Śakuni once more with five smooth-jointed shafts, he smote Ulūka with three, and with three more of solid iron.

sanskrit: tam ulūkas tathā viddhvā vāsudevam atāḍayat nanāda ca mahānādaṃ pūrayan vasudhātalam
english: Ulūka, thus pierced, struck Vāsudeva in return, and roared a mighty roar that filled the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: arjunas tu drutaṃ gatvā śakuner dhanur ācchinat ninye ca caturo vāhān yamasya sadanaṃ prati
english: But Arjuna, advancing swiftly, cut asunder the bow of Śakuni and sent his four steeds toward the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: tato rathād avaplutya saubalo bharatarṣabha ulūkasya rathaṃ tūrṇam āruroha viśāṃ pate
english: Then leaping down from his car, O bull of the Bharatas, the son of Subala swiftly mounted the chariot of Ulūka, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: tāv ekaratham ārūḍhau pitāputrau mahārathau pārthaṃ siṣicatur bāṇair giriṃ meghāv ivotthitau
english: Mounted upon a single car, those two mighty car-warriors, father and son, drenched Pārtha with arrows as two upreared clouds drench a mountain.

sanskrit: tau tu viddhvā mahārāja pāṇḍavo niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ vidrāvayaṃs tava camūṃ śataśo vyadhamac charaiḥ
english: But the Pāṇḍava, having pierced them both, O great king, with sharpened arrows, and routing your host, scattered them by the hundred with his shafts.

sanskrit: anilena yathābhrāṇi vicchinnāni samantataḥ vicchinnāni tathā rājan balāny āsan viśāṃ pate
english: As clouds are scattered on every side by the wind, so were your forces scattered, O king, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: tad balaṃ bharataśreṣṭha vadhyamānaṃ tathā niśi pradudrāva diśaḥ sarvā vīkṣamāṇaṃ bhayārditam
english: That army, O best of the Bharatas, thus being slaughtered in the night, fled in every direction, looking about in its terror, tormented by fear.

sanskrit: utsṛjya vāhān samare codayantas tathāpare saṃbhrāntāḥ paryadhāvanta tasmiṃs tamasi dāruṇe
english: Some abandoned their steeds in the battle, while others, urging them on, ran bewildered hither and thither in that dreadful darkness.

sanskrit: vijitya samare yodhāṃs tāvakān bharatarṣabha dadhmatur muditau śaṅkhau vāsudevadhanaṃjayau
english: Having vanquished your warriors in the battle, O bull of the Bharatas, Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya, full of joy, blew their conches.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārāja droṇaṃ viddhvā tribhiḥ śaraiḥ ciccheda dhanuṣas tūrṇaṃ jyāṃ śareṇa śitena ha
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O great king, having pierced Droṇa with three arrows, swiftly cut the bowstring of his bow with a sharpened shaft.

sanskrit: tan nidhāya dhanur nīḍe droṇaḥ kṣatriyamardanaḥ ādade 'nyad dhanuḥ śūro vegavat sāravattaram
english: Laying that bow aside in its rest, Droṇa, the crusher of warriors, the valiant one, took up another bow, swift and of greater strength.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ tato droṇo viddhvā saptabhir āśugaiḥ sārathiṃ pañcabhir bāṇai rājan vivyādha saṃyuge
english: Then Droṇa, having pierced Dhṛṣṭadyumna with seven swift arrows, struck his charioteer with five shafts, O king, in the fray.

sanskrit: taṃ nivārya śarais tūrṇaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārathaḥ vyadhamat kauravīṃ senāṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Checking him swiftly with arrows, the mighty car-warrior Dhṛṣṭadyumna scattered the Kaurava army by the hundred and by the thousand.

sanskrit: vadhyamāne bale tasmiṃs tava putrasya māriṣa prāvartata nadī ghorā śoṇitaughataraṅgiṇī
english: While that army of your son was being slaughtered, O honored one, a fearful river arose, rolling with waves of streaming blood.

sanskrit: ubhayoḥ senayor madhye narāśvadvipavāhinī yathā vaitaraṇī rājan yamarāṣṭrapuraṃ prati
english: Between the two armies it flowed, bearing along men, horses, and elephants, like the Vaitaraṇī, O king, that runs toward the city of Yama's realm.

sanskrit: drāvayitvā tu tat sainyaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ pratāpavān atyarājata tejasvī śakro devagaṇeṣv iva
english: Having routed that host, the glorious Dhṛṣṭadyumna shone forth in his splendor, as Śakra among the hosts of the gods.

sanskrit: atha dadhmur mahāśaṅkhān dhṛṣṭadyumnaśikhaṇḍinau yamau ca yuyudhānaś ca pāṇḍavaś ca vṛkodaraḥ
english: Then Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, the twins, and Yuyudhāna, and the Pāṇḍava Vṛkodara blew their great conches.

sanskrit: jitvā rathasahasrāṇi tāvakānāṃ mahārathāḥ siṃhanādaravāṃś cakruḥ pāṇḍavā jitakāśinaḥ
english: Having vanquished thousands of your car-warriors, the mighty Pāṇḍava car-warriors, radiant with victory, raised lion-like roars.

sanskrit: paśyatas tava putrasya karṇasya ca madotkaṭāḥ tathā droṇasya śūrasya drauṇeś caiva viśāṃ pate
english: Frenzied with their triumph, they did so before the very eyes of your son, of Karṇa, of the valiant Droṇa, and of Droṇa's son, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vidrutaṃ svabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā vadhyamānaṃ mahātmabhiḥ krodhena mahatāviṣṭaḥ putras tava viśāṃ pate
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing his own army routed and slaughtered by those great-souled ones, your son, O lord of peoples, was overcome with a mighty wrath.

sanskrit: abhyetya sahasā karṇaṃ droṇaṃ ca jayatāṃ varam amarṣavaśam āpanno vākyajño vākyam abravīt
english: Suddenly approaching Karṇa and Droṇa, the foremost of victors, and yielding to his indignation, that knower of speech spoke these words.

sanskrit: bhavadbhyām iha saṃgrāmo kruddhābhyāṃ saṃpravartitaḥ āhave nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā saindhavaṃ savyasācinā
english: By you two, enraged, was this battle set afoot, when you had seen the lord of the Sindhus slain in combat by Savyasācin.

sanskrit: nihanyamānāṃ pāṇḍūnāṃ balena mama vāhinīm bhūtvā tadvijaye śaktāv aśaktāv iva paśyataḥ
english: Yet now, though able to gain the victory there, you look on as though unable, while my host is being slaughtered by the strength of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yady ahaṃ bhavatos tyājyo na vācyo 'smi tadaiva hi āvāṃ pāṇḍusutān saṃkhye jeṣyāva iti mānadau
english: If I am to be forsaken by you, then you should not have said to me, O bestowers of honor: 'We two shall conquer the sons of Pāṇḍu in battle.'

sanskrit: tadaivāhaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā bhavadbhyām anusaṃmatam kṛtavān pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdhaṃ vairaṃ yodhavināśanam
english: It was upon hearing that word, assented to by you both, that I waged with the Pāṇḍavas this enmity that destroys warriors.

sanskrit: yadi nāhaṃ parityājyo bhavadbhyāṃ puruṣarṣabhau yudhyetām anurūpeṇa vikrameṇa suvikramau
english: If I am not to be abandoned by you, O bulls among men, then fight, O mighty heroes, with prowess worthy of you.

sanskrit: vākpratodena tau vīrau praṇunnau tanayena te prāvartayetāṃ tau yuddhaṃ ghaṭṭitāv iva pannagau
english: Goaded by your son with the lash of words, those two heroes set about the fight like two serpents that have been struck.

sanskrit: tatas tau rathināṃ śreṣṭhau sarvalokadhanurdharau śaineyapramukhān pārthān abhidudruvatū raṇe
english: Then those two foremost of car-warriors, the best bowmen in all the world, rushed in battle upon the Pārthas led by the grandson of Śini.

sanskrit: tathaiva sahitāḥ pārthāḥ svena sainyena saṃvṛtāḥ abhyavartanta tau vīrau nardamānau muhur muhuḥ
english: And likewise the Pārthas, gathered together and surrounded by their own host, advanced against those two heroes, roaring again and again.

sanskrit: atha droṇo maheṣvāso daśabhiḥ śinipuṃgavam avidhyat tvaritaṃ kruddhaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Then Droṇa, the great archer, foremost of all bearers of arms, enraged, swiftly pierced the bull of the Śinis with ten shafts.

sanskrit: karṇaś ca daśabhir bāṇaiḥ putraś ca tava saptabhiḥ daśabhir vṛṣasenaś ca saubalaś cāpi saptabhiḥ ete kaurava saṃkrande śaineyaṃ paryavārayan
english: And Karṇa with ten arrows, and your son with seven, and Vṛṣasena with ten, and the son of Subala with seven — these, O Kaurava, beset the grandson of Śini in the tumult.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca samare droṇaṃ nighnantaṃ pāṇḍavīṃ camūm vivyadhuḥ somakās tūrṇaṃ samantāc charavṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: And seeing Droṇa in the battle smiting the Pāṇḍava host, the Somakas swiftly pierced him on every side with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tato droṇo 'harat prāṇān kṣatriyāṇāṃ viśāṃ pate raśmibhir bhāskaro rājaṃs tamasām iva bhārata
english: Then Droṇa bore away the lives of the warriors, O lord of peoples, as the sun with its rays bears away the darkness, O king, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: droṇena vadhyamānānāṃ pāñcālānāṃ viśāṃ pate śuśruve tumulaḥ śabdaḥ krośatām itaretaram
english: From the Pāñcālas being slaughtered by Droṇa, O lord of peoples, there was heard a tumultuous clamor as they cried out to one another.

sanskrit: putrān anye pitṝn anye bhrātṝn anye ca mātulān bhāgineyān vayasyāṃś ca tathā saṃbandhibāndhavān utsṛjyotsṛjya gacchanti tvaritā jīvitepsavaḥ
english: Some abandoning their sons, some their fathers, some their brothers and maternal uncles, some their nephews and comrades, and likewise their kinsmen and friends, they fled in haste, longing to keep their lives.

sanskrit: apare mohitā mohāt tam evābhimukhā yayuḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ raṇe yodhāḥ paralokaṃ tathāpare
english: Others, deluded by their bewilderment, went straight against him; and other warriors of the Pāṇḍavas went thus to the world beyond.

sanskrit: sā tathā pāṇḍavī senā vadhyamānā mahātmabhiḥ niśi saṃprādravad rājann utsṛjyolkāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: That Pāṇḍava army, thus being slaughtered, fled in the night, O king, casting aside their torches by the thousand.

sanskrit: paśyato bhīmasenasya vijayasyācyutasya ca yamayor dharmaputrasya pārṣatasya ca paśyataḥ
english: This took place before the very eyes of Bhīmasena, of Vijaya, of Acyuta, of the twins, of the son of Dharma, and of the son of Pṛṣata as they looked on.

sanskrit: tamasā saṃvṛte loke na prājñāyata kiṃ cana kauravāṇāṃ prakāśena dṛśyante tu drutāḥ pare
english: With the world wrapped in darkness, nothing could be discerned; but by the light of the Kauravas the routed foes were seen.

sanskrit: dravamāṇaṃ tu tat sainyaṃ droṇakarṇau mahārathau jaghnatuḥ pṛṣṭhato rājan kirantau sāyakān bahūn
english: As that host fled, the two mighty car-warriors Droṇa and Karṇa smote them from behind, O king, pouring out many shafts.

sanskrit: pāñcāleṣu prabhagneṣu dīryamāṇeṣu sarvaśaḥ janārdano dīnamanāḥ pratyabhāṣata phalgunam
english: When the Pāñcālas were broken and shattered on every side, Janārdana, with downcast heart, addressed Phalguna in reply.

sanskrit: droṇakarṇau maheṣvāsāv etau pārṣatasātyakī pāñcālāṃś caiva sahitau jaghnatuḥ sāyakair bhṛśam
english: These two great archers, Droṇa and Karṇa, joined together, are sorely smiting the son of Pṛṣata, Sātyaki, and the Pāñcālas with their shafts.

sanskrit: etayoḥ śaravarṣeṇa prabhagnā no mahārathāḥ vāryamāṇāpi kaunteya pṛtanā nāvatiṣṭhate
english: By the arrow-shower of these two our mighty car-warriors are broken; and though I strive to hold them, O son of Kuntī, the army does not stand firm.

sanskrit: etāv āvāṃ sarvasainyair vyūḍhaiḥ samyag udāyudhaiḥ droṇaṃ ca sūtaputraṃ ca prayatāvaḥ prabādhitum
english: Let us two, with all our forces well marshaled and with weapons upraised, make our utmost effort to beat back Droṇa and the son of the charioteer.

sanskrit: etau hi balinau śūrau kṛtāstrau jitakāśinau upekṣitau balaṃ kruddhau nāśayetāṃ niśām imām eṣa bhīmo 'bhiyāty ugraḥ punar āvartya vāhinīm
english: For these two are mighty, valiant, skilled in arms, and radiant with victory; if neglected, in their wrath they would destroy our army this very night. Yonder comes the terrible Bhīma, having rallied his host once more.

sanskrit: vṛkodaraṃ tathāyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra janārdanaḥ punar evābravīd rājan harṣayann iva pāṇḍavam
english: Seeing Vṛkodara thus coming on, Janārdana there, O king, spoke once more, as though gladdening the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: eṣa bhīmo raṇaślāghī vṛtaḥ somakapāṇḍavaiḥ ruṣito 'bhyeti vegena droṇakarṇau mahābalau
english: Yonder Bhīma, glorious in battle, encircled by the Somakas and the Pāṇḍavas, in his fury rushes with speed upon the mighty Droṇa and Karṇa.

sanskrit: etena sahito yudhya pāñcālaiś ca mahārathaiḥ āśvāsanārthaṃ sarveṣāṃ sainyānāṃ pāṇḍunandana
english: Joined with him and with the mighty Pāñcāla car-warriors, do battle, O delight of Pāṇḍu, to bring heart to all the armies.

sanskrit: tatas tau puruṣavyāghrāv ubhau mādhavapāṇḍavau droṇakarṇau samāsādya dhiṣṭhitau raṇamūrdhani
english: Then those two tigers among men, Mādhava and the Pāṇḍava together, having reached Droṇa and Karṇa, took their stand at the head of the battle.

sanskrit: tatas tat punar āvṛttaṃ yudhiṣṭhirabalaṃ mahat tato droṇaś ca karṇaś ca parān mamṛdatur yudhi
english: Then that great army of Yudhiṣṭhira turned back once more; and thereupon Droṇa and Karṇa crushed the foe in the fight.

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāras tumulo niśi pratyabhavan mahān yathā sāgarayo rājaṃś candrodayavivṛddhayoḥ
english: That tumultuous, mighty clash arose in the night, O king, like the meeting of two oceans swollen by the rising of the moon.

sanskrit: tata utsṛjya pāṇibhyaḥ pradīpāṃs tava vāhinī yuyudhe pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdham unmattavad ahaḥkṣaye
english: Then, casting the lamps from their hands, your army fought against the Pāṇḍavas like madmen at the dying of the day.

sanskrit: rajasā tamasā caiva saṃvṛte bhṛśadāruṇe kevalaṃ nāmagotreṇa prāyudhyanta jayaiṣiṇaḥ
english: With all enveloped by dust and by darkness, exceedingly dreadful, those who sought victory fought only by name and lineage.

sanskrit: aśrūyanta hi nāmāni śrāvyamāṇāni pārthivaiḥ praharadbhir mahārāja svayaṃvara ivāhave
english: For the names proclaimed by the kings as they smote were heard, O great king, in that battle as at a self-choice ceremony.

sanskrit: niḥśabdam āsīt sahasā punaḥ śabdo mahān abhūt kruddhānāṃ yudhyamānānāṃ jayatāṃ jīyatām api
english: All at once there was silence; then again a mighty din arose of those enraged and fighting, of the victors and the vanquished alike.

sanskrit: yatra yatra sma dṛśyante pradīpāḥ kurusattama tatra tatra sma te śūrā nipatanti pataṃgavat
english: Wherever lamps were seen, O best of the Kurus, there those heroes fell upon them like moths.

sanskrit: tathā saṃyudhyamānānāṃ vigāḍhābhūn mahāniśā pāṇḍavānāṃ ca rājendra kauravāṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: As they thus fought, the deep night advanced, O lord of kings, upon the Pāṇḍavas and the Kauravas on every side.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ karṇo raṇe dṛṣṭvā pārṣataṃ paravīrahā ājaghānorasi śarair daśabhir marmabhedibhiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Karṇa, slayer of hostile heroes, beholding the son of Pṛṣata in the battle, struck him on the breast with ten arrows that pierce the vital parts.

sanskrit: prativivyādha taṃ tūrṇaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumno 'pi māriṣa pañcabhiḥ sāyakair hṛṣṭas tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna too, O honored one, pierced him swiftly in return with five shafts, and joyously cried, 'Stand, stand!'

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ śaraiḥ saṃkhye saṃchādya sumahārathau punaḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭair vivyadhāte parasparam
english: Those two great car-warriors, having covered each other with arrows in the fray, again pierced one another with shafts loosed at full stretch.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāñcālamukhyasya dhṛṣṭadyumnasya saṃyuge sārathiṃ caturaś cāśvān karṇo vivyādha sāyakaiḥ
english: Then in the fight Karṇa pierced with his shafts the charioteer and the four steeds of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the chief of the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: kārmukapravaraṃ cāsya praciccheda śitaiḥ śaraiḥ sārathiṃ cāsya bhallena rathanīḍād apātayat
english: And he cut asunder his excellent bow with sharpened arrows, and with a broad-headed shaft felled his charioteer from the body of the car.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu viratho hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ gṛhītvā parighaṃ ghoraṃ karṇasyāśvān apīpiṣat
english: But Dhṛṣṭadyumna, his car destroyed, his steeds slain and his charioteer slain, seizing a fearful iron club, crushed the horses of Karṇa.

sanskrit: viddhaś ca bahubhis tena śarair āśīviṣopamaiḥ tato yudhiṣṭhirānīkaṃ padbhyām evānvavartata āruroha rathaṃ cāpi sahadevasya māriṣa
english: And pierced by him with many arrows like venomous serpents, he then made his way on foot to the host of Yudhiṣṭhira, and mounted the car of Sahadeva, O honored one.

sanskrit: karṇasyāpi rathe vāhān anyān sūto nyayojayat śaṅkhavarṇān mahāvegān saindhavān sādhuvāhinaḥ
english: To the car of Karṇa, too, the charioteer yoked other steeds, conch-colored, of great swiftness, born of the Sindhu country, and well-trained to draw.

sanskrit: labdhalakṣyas tu rādheyaḥ pāñcālānāṃ mahārathān abhyapīḍayad āyastaḥ śarair megha ivācalān
english: And Rādheya, having found his mark, strove hard and pressed the mighty car-warriors of the Pāñcālas with his arrows as a cloud presses the mountains.

sanskrit: sā pīḍyamānā karṇena pāñcālānāṃ mahācamūḥ saṃprādravat susaṃtrastā siṃhenevārditā mṛgī
english: That great host of the Pāñcālas, sorely pressed by Karṇa, fled away in utter terror, like a doe tormented by a lion.

sanskrit: patitās turagebhyaś ca gajebhyaś ca mahītale rathebhyaś ca narās tūrṇam adṛśyanta tatas tataḥ
english: Men fallen swiftly from horses and from elephants to the ground, and from chariots, were seen here and there.

sanskrit: dhāvamānasya yodhasya kṣurapraiḥ sa mahāmṛdhe bāhū ciccheda vai karṇaḥ śiraś caiva sakuṇḍalam
english: With razor-edged shafts in that great battle Karṇa cut off the arms of one warrior as he fled, and his head as well, with its earrings.

sanskrit: ūrū ciccheda cānyasya gajasthasya viśāṃ pate vājipṛṣṭhagatasyāpi bhūmiṣṭhasya ca māriṣa
english: And he cut off the thighs of another seated upon an elephant, O lord of peoples, and of one mounted on the back of a horse, and of one standing on the ground, O honored one.

sanskrit: nājñāsiṣur dhāvamānā bahavaś ca mahārathāḥ saṃchinnāny ātmagātrāṇi vāhanāni ca saṃyuge
english: Many a mighty car-warrior fleeing did not even perceive that his own limbs and his mounts had been severed in the fight.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare pāñcālāḥ sṛñjayaiḥ saha tṛṇapraspandanāc cāpi sūtaputraṃ sma menire
english: Those Pāñcālas, slaughtered in the battle together with the Sṛñjayas, fancied the son of the charioteer present even at the mere stirring of a blade of grass.

sanskrit: api svaṃ samare yodhaṃ dhāvamānaṃ vicetasaḥ karṇam evābhyamanyanta tato bhītā dravanti te
english: Bereft of their senses, they took even their own fleeing warrior in the battle to be Karṇa himself, and so in their terror they fled.

sanskrit: tāny anīkāni bhagnāni dravamāṇāni bhārata abhyadravad drutaṃ karṇaḥ pṛṣṭhato vikirañ śarān
english: Those broken divisions as they fled, O Bhārata, Karṇa swiftly pursued from behind, scattering his arrows.

sanskrit: avekṣamāṇās te 'nyonyaṃ susaṃmūḍhā vicetasaḥ nāśaknuvann avasthātuṃ kālyamānā mahātmanā
english: Gazing at one another, utterly bewildered and senseless, they were unable to hold their ground, harried as they were by that great-souled one.
